question: Why are three rows said to exist above the aṇimā group?
premises: Above the worlds beginning with aṇimā there are three rows.
These rows pertain to teacher and disciple.
Their threefoldness is explained by association with the shadow of the three guṇas.
inference: The triadic structure of those higher rows reflects the influence of the three guṇas.
uncertainties: The term paṅkti may refer to series, channels, or grouped worlds depending on context.
plain_english: Above the worlds beginning with aṇimā there are three rows connected with teacher and disciple. Their threefold division is explained by the influence of the three qualities.
